mainTopic: Redeeming houses in walled cities (בתי ערי חומה): heirs, resale, leap years, gifts, הקדש, יובל, and הלל's תקנה
overview: This amud opens with רבא explaining an earlier argument about interest. Everyone forbids צד אחד ברבית, and the real argument is about רבית על מנת להחזיר. The גמרא then works through the משנה on houses in walled cities. The words 'וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ' teach that the right to redeem passes to the seller's son and works against the buyer's son. The redemption year is counted from the first sale, and רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן argue over which buyer keeps the house forever. רבי אבא בר ממל shows that in a leap year the extra month counts, both for houses and for the age of lambs. רבי and the חכמים disagree about how long a 'full year' is. The word לצמיתות teaches that the house becomes the buyer's forever and that a gift is included, which the גמרא concludes is not רבי מאיר's view. A ברייתא then explains a house given to הקדש, and רב ספרא explains why the יובל does not return the house. Finally, a new משנה tells of הלל's תקנה against buyers who hid, and רבא learns from it that a conditional גט needs the husband to accept the money willingly.

steps.title: רבא explains the argument differently
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both sides agree that צד אחד ברבית is forbidden. They argue only about רבית על מנת להחזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees that uncertain interest is forbidden. Here, the argument is about interest given on the condition that it will be returned. One master holds it is forbidden, and the other holds it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers his own explanation of what the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה are arguing about in the earlier ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier approach said the argument was about צד אחד ברבית, a deal that might turn out to be interest and might not. רבא rejects that: on this point there is no argument, and everyone forbids it. In his view they argue about a deal where any benefit that turns out to be interest will be paid back. One side still forbids it, and the other permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One-sided interest'. A deal that may or may not end up being interest, depending on what happens later.
Interest taken on the condition that it will be returned if it turns out to be interest.
Everyone, meaning all the opinions agree.
This is the difference between them.
One master holds. Used to show each side of an argument.

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying that uncertain interest is allowed. He is saying the opposite: everyone forbids it, so it cannot be what they argue about.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא צַד אֶחָד בְּרִבִּית אָסוּר,
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that uncertain interest is forbidden,
and here, interest on the condition that it be returned
is the difference between them:
one master holds it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא of the earlier ברייתא.

phrases.english: and one master holds it is permitted.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא צַד אֶחָד בְּרִבִּית אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation of the earlier argument, replacing the view that it was about צד אחד ברבית.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the argument is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about צד אחד ברבית.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone forbids צד אחד ברבית. The argument is only about רבית על מנת להחזיר.

steps.title: If the seller dies his son redeems, but isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a dead seller's son may redeem the house, and asks why this needs to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If the seller died, his son may redeem. That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks why it bothers to teach something that seems obvious. A son inherits his father's rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A son normally takes over all of his father's property and rights. So it seems clear that he may redeem the house his father sold. The question pushes the גמרא to find a reason why we might have thought otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: The seller, the original owner of the house.
He may redeem, meaning buy back the house.
It is obvious! The גמרא asks why a clear rule needs to be stated.

phrases.english: The משנה said: If the seller died, his son may redeem.
That is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת הַמּוֹכֵר יִגְאַל בְּנוֹ. פְּשִׁיטָא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to say that the seller's son may redeem
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A son inherits his father's rights, so the rule seems too obvious to need saying.

steps.title: The son redeems even though he did not sell
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought only the man who sold the house may redeem it. The words 'וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ' teach that the right exists in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: The Torah said 'And if a man sells a dwelling house', and this son did not sell. So the Torah teaches us: 'He shall have the right of redemption', meaning in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה needed to teach this rule. It also shows where in the Torah the son's right comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a man who sells a house and then redeems it. That might suggest only the seller himself can redeem. The extra words 'וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ' widen the right, so his son can redeem too.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. Introduces a mistaken idea we could have had.
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah.
It teaches us. Introduces the correct point.
'He shall have the right of redemption.'
In any case, in every situation.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְאִישׁ כִּי יִמְכֹּר בֵּית מוֹשַׁב״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא,
phrases.english: the Torah said 'And if a man sells a dwelling house',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:29

phrases.english: and this son did not sell,
so it teaches us:
'He shall have the right of redemption', meaning in any case.
phrases.notes: These words are from the same פסוק, ויקרא 25:29.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: וְאִישׁ כִּי יִמְכֹּר בֵּית מוֹשַׁב אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows a reasonable mistake and the פסוק that rules it out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the man who actually sold may redeem, since the פסוק says 'a man sells'.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ' means the right of redemption applies in any case, even to the seller's son.

steps.title: If the buyer dies, redeem from his son, but isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next rule of the משנה, that the house can be redeemed from a dead buyer's son, and again asks why it needs saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If the buyer died, the seller may redeem the house from his son, and so on. That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and asks the same question: isn't this obvious?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer's son simply inherits whatever his father had. That includes a house that can still be redeemed. So it seems clear the seller may redeem it from the son.

keyTerms.meaning: The buyer.
From the hand of his son, meaning out of the son's possession.
Short for 'and so on'. The quote of the משנה continues.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת הַלּוֹקֵחַ יִגְאַל מִיָּד בְּנוֹ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: The משנה said: If the buyer died, the seller may redeem from his son, and so on.
That is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת הַלּוֹקֵחַ יִגְאַל מִיָּד בְּנוֹ וְכוּ׳. פְּשִׁיטָא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 2, now applied to the buyer's side.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to say the house can be redeemed from the buyer's son
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An heir steps into his father's position, so of course the house can still be redeemed from him.

steps.title: Redemption works even from someone who did not buy
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought the right only works against the actual buyer. 'וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ' teaches that it applies in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: The Torah said 'to the one who bought it', and this son did not buy. So it teaches us: 'He shall have the right of redemption', meaning in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer as before. This time the mistake comes from a word that describes the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'the one who bought it' (לקונה אותו). That might suggest the redemption only works against the actual buyer, not his heir. The words 'וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ' again make the right apply in any case, even against the son.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To the one who bought it.' The פסוק's description of the buyer.
He did not buy.

steps.whatToRemember: Both of these lines of the משנה come from the same words, 'וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ' (in any case). The right to redeem passes to the seller's heirs, and it also works against the buyer's heirs.

phrases.english: You might have said:
the Torah said 'to the one who bought it',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:30

phrases.english: and this son did not buy,
so it teaches us:
'He shall have the right of redemption', meaning in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: לַקּוֹנֶה אוֹתוֹ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question of step 4, in the same way as step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows a reasonable mistake and the פסוק that rules it out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The house can only be redeemed from the actual buyer, since the פסוק says 'the one who bought it'.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וְהָיְתָה גְּאֻלָּתוֹ' makes the right apply in any case, even against the buyer's son.

steps.title: The year is counted from the first sale
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the year for redeeming is counted from the time the owner sold the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: One counts the year for him only from the time that he sold, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up a ברייתא that shows where the rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the buyer resells the house to someone else. Does the one year for redeeming start over? The משנה says no: the year runs from the original owner's sale.

keyTerms.meaning: One does not count.
Year. Here, the one year in which a house in a walled city may be redeemed.
From the time that he sold.

phrases.english: The משנה said: One counts the year for him
only from the time that he sold, and so on.
phrases.notes: The משנה is talking about a case where the buyer then sold the house to a second buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוֹנִין לוֹ שָׁנָה אֶלָּא מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁמָּכַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The redemption year is counted from the original sale.

steps.title: Which sale starts the year?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks whether the word 'year' means a year from the first sale or from the second sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'Year'. I do not know whether it means a year from the sale to the first buyer or a year from the sale to the second buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a question: when the house has been sold twice, from which sale do we count the year?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'year' by itself does not say when the count starts. If it starts from the second sale, a resale would give the original owner extra time. The ברייתא sets up this doubt so it can settle it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not know. Introduces a doubt in reading the פסוק.
The first buyer.
The second buyer.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
'Year': I do not know
whether it means a year from the sale to the first buyer
or a year from the sale to the second buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שָׁנָה — אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם שָׁנָה לָרִאשׁוֹן אִם שָׁנָה לַשֵּׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to find the source of the משנה's rule in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the redemption year is counted from the first sale or from the second sale.

steps.title: 'A full year for him' means from the first sale
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves from the words 'עד מלאת לו שנה תמימה' that the year is counted from the first sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק says 'until the passage of a full year for him', you must say it is a year from the sale to the first buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question using the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the words 'for him' (לו) as pointing to the original seller. The year belongs to him, so it starts from his sale to the first buyer. This is the source for the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: When it says. Introduces a proof from the פסוק.
A full, complete year.
It is, so you must say.

steps.whatToRemember: A resale does not restart the clock. The original owner has one year from his own sale to redeem a house in a walled city.

phrases.english: When the פסוק says
'until the passage of a full year for him',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:30. 'For him' (לו) means the original seller.

phrases.english: it must be a year from the sale to the first buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר עַד מְלֹאת לוֹ שָׁנָה תְמִימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the doubt raised in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The year is counted from the original owner's sale to the first buyer, based on the word 'לו' in the פסוק.

steps.title: Whose house is it forever?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who owns the house permanently once the year from the first sale ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: To whom does the house belong forever?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question that follows from the last step. If the year is counted from the first sale, who owns the house permanently once that year is over? This sets up the argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner sold the house to a first buyer, who then sold it to a second buyer. We already know the clock started at the first sale. Now we need to know which buyer gets to keep the house forever.

keyTerms.meaning: Permanently owned. The house can no longer be bought back.

phrases.english: To whom is it permanently owned?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמִי חָלוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question that comes out of the ruling that the year counts from the first sale.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which buyer becomes the permanent owner when the year from the first sale ends.

steps.title: The argument: first buyer or second buyer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the first buyer owns it forever. רבי יוחנן says the second buyer does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says it belongs forever to the first buyer. רבי יוחנן says it belongs forever to the second buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר gives the house to the first buyer, because the year was counted from his purchase. רבי יוחנן gives it to the second buyer. The גמרא asks for his reason in the next step and answers it in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: The first buyer
The second buyer, who bought the house from the first buyer

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
It is permanently owned by the first buyer,
Rabbi Yochanan says:
It is permanently owned by the second buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: לָרִאשׁוֹן חָלוּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposite answers to the question in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: the first buyer owns it permanently. רבי יוחנן: the second buyer owns it permanently.

steps.title: What is רבי יוחנן's reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר makes sense, since the year was counted for the first buyer. But why would רבי יוחנן give the house to the second buyer?
steps.simpleTranslation: We understand רבי אלעזר, because we count the year according to the first buyer. But according to רבי יוחנן, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבי אלעזר's view as logical. It then challenges רבי יוחנן to explain himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The year was counted from the first buyer's purchase, so it seems natural that the permanent ownership is his. רבי יוחנן gives it to the second buyer instead, and the גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for (one side). This opens a contrast with a side that is harder to understand.
What is the reason?
We count

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Rabbi Elazar,
since we count the year according to him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the first buyer. Step 8 proved the year runs from his purchase.

phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Yochanan, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דִּלְדִידֵיהּ קָא מָנֵינַן, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's side of the argument in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the second buyer owns the house permanently
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The year is counted from the first buyer's purchase, so the permanent ownership should be his.

steps.title: The first buyer sold every right he would get
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל explains that the first buyer sold the second buyer every right that would come to him, including permanent ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל said: What did the first buyer sell to the second? Every right that would come into his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל defends רבי יוחנן. The first buyer handed over all of his rights to the house, including the right to own it permanently later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the year counts from the first sale. But when the house becomes permanent, that permanent ownership is a right the first buyer already sold to the second buyer. So it goes to the second buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: A right or benefit in the property

steps.whatToRemember: The year counts from the first sale, but according to רבי יוחנן the permanent ownership goes to the second buyer. This is because the first buyer sold him all of his future rights.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel said:
What did the first buyer sell to the second?
Every right that will come into his hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה מָכַר לוֹ רִאשׁוֹן לְשֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reasoning of the challenged opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the year is counted for the first buyer, the permanent ownership should belong to him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first buyer sold all of his future rights, so the permanent ownership passes to the second buyer.

steps.title: Two houses sold in a leap year
steps.stepSummary: A house sold on 15 אדר הראשון becomes permanent only on 15 אדר of next year. A house sold on 1 אדר השני becomes permanent already on 1 אדר of next year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל said: Someone sold two houses in walled cities. He sold one on the 15th of אדר הראשון and one on the 1st of אדר השני. The one sold in אדר השני completes its year when the 1st of אדר next year arrives. The one sold on the 15th of אדר הראשון does not complete its year until the 15th of אדר next year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל teaches a new rule about counting the year in a leap year, which has two months of אדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The year is counted to the same date in the next year, so the extra month counts. The house sold in אדר הראשון needs about thirteen months. The house sold later, in אדר השני, needs only twelve, so it becomes permanent sooner.

keyTerms.meaning: Houses in walled cities, which can be bought back only within one year
The first אדר, the extra month added in a leap year
The second אדר in a leap year
His year has been completed

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards, but the house sold later becomes permanent earlier. The extra month counts as part of the year for the house sold in אדר הראשון.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel said:
If one sold two houses in walled cities,
one on the fifteenth of the first Adar
and one on the first of the second Adar;
the one he sold him in the second Adar,
once the first day
of Adar of the next year arrives,
his year is complete;

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁמָּכַר לוֹ בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר שֶׁל אֲדָר הָרִאשׁוֹן —
phrases.english: the one he sold him on the fifteenth of the first Adar,
his year is not complete

phrases.aramaic: עַד חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בַּאֲדָר שֶׁל שָׁנָה הַבָּאָה.
phrases.english: until the fifteenth of Adar of the next year.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָכַר שְׁנֵי בָּתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching about how the year is counted in a leap year.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a leap year, a house sold on 1 אדר השני becomes permanent on 1 אדר of the next year. A house sold on 15 אדר הראשון becomes permanent only on 15 אדר of the next year.

steps.title: "I lit my fire before you!"
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks: the first buyer bought before the second buyer, so how can the second buyer's house become permanent first?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged this: Let the first buyer say to the second, "I came before you and lit my fire before yours!"
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רבי אבא בר ממל's ruling. It seems unfair that the person who bought first should finish his year last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer from אדר הראשון bought earlier, so he should be able to say that his year started first. Then his house should become permanent first.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it
Lit a fire. This is a way of saying "I started first."

phrases.english: Ravina challenged it:
But let him say to him:
phrases.notes: The first buyer, who bought in אדר הראשון, would be speaking to the buyer from אדר השני.

phrases.english: "I came first and lit a fire
before yours!"

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא בר ממל's rule that the later sale becomes permanent first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whoever bought earlier started his year earlier, so his year should end earlier too.

steps.title: "You went into the extra month"
steps.stepSummary: The second buyer can answer that the first buyer bought during the extra month, so his year has thirteen months.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the second buyer can say to him: "You went down into the extra month."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבינא. The first buyer's year includes the extra month, so it is longer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Starting earlier does not help when your year is longer. The extra month counts toward the year, so the buyer from אדר הראשון has to wait thirteen months, while the buyer from אדר השני waits only twelve.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra month added to make a leap year

steps.whatToRemember: In a leap year the extra month counts as part of the year. A sale in אדר הראשון needs thirteen months before the house becomes permanent.

phrases.english: Because he can say to him:
"You went down into the extra month."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַתְּ נְחֵית לְעִיבּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a factor the challenger left out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The buyer who started first should finish first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The earlier buyer's year includes the extra month, so it is longer and ends later.

steps.title: Two lambs born in a leap year
steps.stepSummary: The same counting applies to the age of lambs. A lamb born on 1 אדר השני turns one on 1 אדר. A lamb born on 15 אדר הראשון turns one only on 15 אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל also said: Two lambs were born to someone. One was born on the 15th of אדר הראשון and one on the 1st of אדר השני. The one born in אדר השני completes its year when the 1st of אדר next year arrives. The one born on the 15th of אדר הראשון does not complete its year until the 15th of אדר next year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל applies the same leap-year counting to the age of animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal's age matters for הלכות that depend on it being within its first year, such as קרבנות. Here too the extra month counts. So the lamb born earlier, in אדר הראשון, reaches one year later than the lamb born in אדר השני.

keyTerms.meaning: Lambs
Were born

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abba bar Memel said:
If two lambs were born to him,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר שֶׁל אֲדָר הָרִאשׁוֹן
phrases.english: one on the fifteenth of the first Adar
and one on the first of the second Adar,
the one born in the second Adar,
once the first day
of Adar of the next year arrives,
its year is complete,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁנּוֹלַד לוֹ בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בַּאֲדָר הָרִאשׁוֹן —
phrases.english: the one born to him on the fifteenth of the first Adar,
its year is not complete

phrases.aramaic: עַד חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בַּאֲדָר שֶׁל שָׁנָה הַבָּאָה.
phrases.english: until the fifteenth of Adar of the next year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל: נוֹלְדוּ לוֹ שְׁנֵי טְלָאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same leap-year counting from the houses to the age of animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lamb born on 1 אדר השני turns one on 1 אדר of the next year. A lamb born on 15 אדר הראשון turns one only on 15 אדר of the next year.

steps.title: רבינא asks: shouldn't the older lamb turn one first?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges the lamb rule: the lamb born first should be able to say it is older.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objected: Let the first lamb say to the second one: I started eating grass before you did!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the rule from the last step, where the lamb born later turns one year old first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lamb born on 15 אדר הראשון was born before the lamb born on 1 אדר השני. So it seems backward that the younger lamb reaches one year first. רבינא pictures the older lamb arguing: I was here first.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects, raises a strong challenge
Grass, greens (here a picture for 'I was born first')
Came first, preceded

phrases.english: Ravina objects to this:
But let [the first lamb] say to [the second]:
I came first and ate grass
before you!
phrases.notes: Eating grass first is a picture. He means 'I was born before you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מתקיף לה רבינא, ולימא ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the lamb-age rule from step 16, just like רבינא attacked the house rule in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a lamb born on 1 אדר השני turns one before a lamb born on 15 אדר הראשון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The lamb born earlier is older, so it seems it should reach one year first.

steps.title: The older lamb was born in the extra month
steps.stepSummary: The second lamb answers: you were born during the extra month, so your year is longer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the second lamb can say to it: You came down into the world during the extra month; I did not come down during the extra month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבינא with the same idea it used for the houses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first lamb was born in אדר הראשון, the extra month added to a leap year. So its first year has thirteen months. The second lamb was born after the extra month, so its year is only twelve months and ends sooner.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra month added in a leap year
You came down (you were born)

phrases.english: Because [the second] can say to it:
You came down during the extra month,
I did not come down during the extra month.

steps.triggerLanguage: משום דאמר ליה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the rule makes sense: being born first does not matter when your year includes the extra month.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lamb born earlier must reach one year first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lamb born in the extra month has a thirteen-month year, so the later lamb can turn one first.

steps.title: Why teach the lamb rule if it matches the house rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the lamb rule was needed, since it seems to be the same as the house rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this one too? It is the same as that one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אבא בר ממל needed to say the lamb rule. It looks like an exact copy of the house rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rules count a year the same way when there is an extra month. If we already know it for houses, saying it again for lambs seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it?
This is the same as that
Also, again

phrases.english: Why do I need this one too?
It is the same as that!

steps.triggerLanguage: הא תו למה לי? היינו הך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back and questions why step 16 was said at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the lamb rule in step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the lamb rule is identical to the house rule, repeating it adds nothing.

steps.title: The word 'year' links lambs to houses
steps.stepSummary: Without the lamb rule we might think only houses count this way, because only there the תורה says 'full.' The word 'year' in both places links them.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: There, by houses, where it says 'full,' the rule applies; here, by lambs, where it does not say 'full,' it does not. So it teaches us that 'year' and 'year' are learned from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the lamb rule does teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By houses the פסוק says a 'full' year (תמימה), so we might think the extra month counts only there. By lambs that word is missing. The lamb rule teaches that the word 'year' appears in both places, so the two cases teach each other, and lambs follow the same counting.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought
So it teaches us
Full, complete (said about the year for houses)
They are learned from each other

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a rule which looks repeated can be teaching that one case is linked to another through a shared word.

phrases.english: You might have said:
There, where 'full' is written,
phrases.notes: 'There' means houses in walled cities: ויקרא 25:30.

phrases.english: here, where 'full' is not written, no.
So it teaches us
that 'year' and 'year' are learned from each other.
phrases.notes: The lamb's 'year' is in שמות 12:5.

steps.triggerLanguage: מהו דתימא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the second rule adds new information: it links the two cases through a shared word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only houses, where the פסוק says 'full,' count the extra month this way; lambs might not.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'year' links both cases, so lambs follow the same counting as houses.
steps.whatToRemember: Houses in walled cities and the age of lambs are counted the same way in a leap year, because the word 'year' links them.

steps.title: How long is a 'full year'? רבי and the חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and brings a ברייתא: רבי counts 365 days, and the חכמים count twelve months, or thirteen in a leap year.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: When it says 'full,' etc. רבי says: to give the year and its extra. The Rabbis taught: 'A full year.' רבי says: He counts 365 days, like the number of days in a sun year. The חכמים say: He counts twelve months from day to day, and if the year got an extra month, it got the extra month for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It quotes the משנה and then brings a ברייתא that spells out what רבי means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, a 'full year' means a sun year of 365 days, which is longer than twelve moon months. For the חכמים, it means twelve months counted from the exact date. If a month is added that year, the seller gets thirteen months to buy back his house.

keyTerms.meaning: The year with its added time
Days of the sun year (365 days)
From this date to the same date
The year was given an extra month

steps.confusionAlert: The two views do not always give the same amount of time. רבי always gives a sun year of 365 days, which is longer than twelve moon months. The חכמים give exactly twelve months from date to date in a normal year. Only in a leap year do they give a thirteenth month.

phrases.english: When it says 'full,' etc.
רבי says:
to give the year and its extra.
The Rabbis taught: 'A full year':
רבי says: he counts
three hundred sixty-five days,
like the number of days in a sun year.
And the חכמים say:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹנֶה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ מִיּוֹם לְיוֹם,
phrases.english: he counts twelve months, from date to date,
and if the year got an extra month,
it got the extra month for him.
phrases.notes: 'For him' means for the seller. He gets the extra month to buy back his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: כשהוא אומר תמימה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה, about what 'full year' means.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: a full year is 365 days. חכמים: twelve months from date to date, and thirteen if the year has an extra month.

steps.title: 'Permanently' means completely and forever
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the end of the year, and a ברייתא explains that לצמיתות means the house belongs to the buyer completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: The last day of the twelve months came and the house was not bought back, etc. The Rabbis taught: 'Permanently' means completely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about what happens when the year ends. It brings a ברייתא to explain the word לצמיתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the year passes and the seller has not bought the house back, the house is fully the buyer's. לצמיתות means this is total and final, not a temporary sale.

keyTerms.meaning: Bought back (redeemed)
Permanently, forever
Completely, with no way back

phrases.english: The last day of the twelve months came
and it was not bought back, etc.
The Rabbis taught: 'Permanently'
phrases.notes: This word is from ויקרא 25:30.

phrases.english: means completely.

steps.triggerLanguage: הגיע יום שנים עשר חודש ולא נגאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the year, the house belongs to the buyer completely and forever.

steps.title: 'Permanently' also includes a house given as a gift
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: the word לצמיתות comes to include a house that was given as a present.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'Permanently' comes to include a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second thing the word לצמיתות teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Besides meaning 'forever,' the word teaches that the same rule applies to a house that was given as a gift, not only to a house that was sold. So someone who received a house in a walled city as a gift also keeps it forever after the year.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation
To include
A gift

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'Permanently'
comes to include a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: דבר אחר לצמיתות לרבות את המתנה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second thing learned from the same word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house in a walled city given as a gift follows the same rule as a sold house.

steps.title: How the word shows that gifts are included
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we learn gifts from this word. It answers that the פסוק used the longer form צמיתות instead of the shorter צמית.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? צמית versus צמיתות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where in the word we see that gifts are included, and answers briefly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The short form צמית would have been enough to say 'forever.' The תורה wrote the longer צמיתות, and the extra letters come to include another case: a gift.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The shorter form of the word 'permanent'

steps.whatToRemember: לצמיתות teaches two things: after the year the house is the buyer's forever, and the same rule covers a house given as a gift.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
'Tzemit,' 'tzemitut.'
phrases.notes: The פסוק could have used the short word צמית. The longer word adds something: gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי טעמא? צמית צמיתות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how step 23's teaching comes out of the word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the word לצמיתות shows that a gift is included.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The longer form צמיתות, instead of the short צמית, adds the case of a gift.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the ברייתא about gifts?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רב פפא: the ברייתא includes a gift, so it cannot be רבי מאיר, who says a gift is not like a sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said this ברייתא in front of רב פפא and asked: whose opinion is it? It does not seem to be רבי מאיר. If it were רבי מאיר, there is a problem, because he says a gift is not like a sale!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who wrote the ברייתא from step 23, which says a house given as a present also becomes the receiver's forever. It points out that this seems to clash with רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that a gift is not treated like a sale. The ברייתא treats a gift exactly like a sale. So it looks like the ברייתא cannot be his view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (whose opinion is this?)
A gift
A sale
Is not like a sale

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rav Pappa:
According to whom?
It is not like Rabbi Meir,
for if it were like Rabbi Meir —
doesn't he say that a gift is not like a sale!
phrases.notes: He says this about a field going back to its owner at יובל: a field given as a gift does not go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who the author is of the ברייתא that includes a gift.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא wrote the ברייתא, given that it seems to clash with רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רב פפא: it can still be רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that it can even be רבי מאיר, because here the Torah specially included a gift with the word לצמיתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: You can even say it is רבי מאיר. This case is different, because the Torah included a gift with the word לצמיתות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends the idea that the ברייתא can follow רבי מאיר. He says the house case is special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In general רבי מאיר holds a gift is not like a sale. But here the פסוק used the extra-long word לצמיתות, which adds in gifts. So even רבי מאיר would agree in this one case.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (this fits even that opinion)
Here it is different
The Torah included (added it in)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
You can even say it is Rabbi Meir;
here it is different,
because the Merciful One included it with "latzemitut."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, שָׁאנֵי הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by saying the house case is an exception.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special verse makes this case different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי מאיר says a gift is not like a sale, the ברייתא cannot be his.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי מאיר agrees here, because the word לצמיתות includes a gift.

steps.title: Challenge from יובל, where gifts are also included
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא is challenged: at יובל the Torah also includes gifts with the word תשובו, and still רבי מאיר does not include them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said to רב פפא, and some say it was רב הונא son of רב יהושע who said to רב פפא: But look at יובל. It is written תשובו, "you shall return," and the חכמים learn from it to include a gift. Yet רבי מאיר does not include a gift there!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא's answer is attacked. The challenger shows that an extra word in the Torah does not make רבי מאיר include gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said a special word in the פסוק would make רבי מאיר agree. But at יובל there is also a special word, תשובו, and רבי מאיר still says gifts do not return. So a special word is not enough to change his view.

keyTerms.meaning: The fiftieth year, when fields go back to their first owners
You shall return
To include (add in)
But look (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: The Sages said to Rav Pappa,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to Rav Pappa:
But regarding the Jubilee,
where it is written "you shall return"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:13

phrases.english: to include the gift,
and Rabbi Meir does not include it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא גַּבֵּי יוֹבֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that a special word would make רבי מאיר include gifts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: At יובל there is also a word that includes gifts, and רבי מאיר still does not include them.

steps.title: The ברייתא is not רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is certainly not like רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this ברייתא is certainly not like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב פפא's answer and settles the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a special word did not change רבי מאיר's view at יובל, it would not change it here either. So the ברייתא that includes a gift must follow the חכמים who argue with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we take back the earlier idea)
Certainly

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא that treats a gifted house in a walled city like a sold one does not follow רבי מאיר, who holds that a gift is not like a sale.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָא וַדַּאי דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: Rather, this is certainly not like Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא וַדַּאי דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge and closes the question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא is not רבי מאיר's view.

steps.title: A house in a walled city given to הקדש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: someone who gives a walled-city house to הקדש can always redeem it. If another person redeems it and the owner does not buy it back within twelve months, it becomes that person's forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If someone gives a house in a walled city to הקדש, he can redeem it, and he can redeem it forever. If someone else redeemed it from הקדש, and the twelve-month day arrived without it being redeemed, it becomes his forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about a walled-city house that was given to הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a regular sale, the seller has only one year to buy the house back. With הקדש, the owner never loses the right to redeem. But once a different person buys it out of הקדש, the normal one-year rule starts working again.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives something to the בית המקדש
Houses in cities with walls
Redeems (buys back)
The property of the בית המקדש
Owned completely and forever

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who consecrates a house among the houses of walled cities —
he may redeem it,
and he may redeem it forever.
If another person redeemed it from the Temple treasury,
and the day of twelve months arrived
and it was not redeemed —
it becomes his forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ בַּיִת בְּבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about a house given to הקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner can always redeem from הקדש. If another person redeems it and a year passes, it is that person's forever.

steps.title: Where do we learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the Torah source of the rule it just quoted. This sets up שמואל's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a rule but no source. The גמרא wants to know which words in the פסוק teach that the one-year rule works even for someone who bought from הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these things known?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the rule that a buyer from הקדש keeps the house forever after a year.

steps.title: שמואל: "to the one who bought it"
steps.stepSummary: שמואל learns it from the words לקונה אותו: anyone who bought the house, even from הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The פסוק says "to the one who bought it," and that means even someone who bought it from הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the source. The words "the one who bought it" cover any buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say "the one who bought it from the owner." It just says "the one who bought it." So a person who bought it out of הקדש is included, and after a year the house is his forever.

keyTerms.meaning: To the one who bought it
From the hand (ownership) of הקדש
For the פסוק says

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
For the verse says: "to the one who bought it,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:30

phrases.english: and even from the Temple treasury.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״לַקּוֹנֶה אוֹתוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words לקונה אותו include a buyer from הקדש.

steps.title: Why doesn't הקדש keep it forever?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the owner does not redeem within a year, let the house belong to הקדש forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let הקדש keep it forever?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first part of the ברייתא, which said the owner can always redeem from הקדש. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If any buyer keeps the house forever after a year, הקדש should be like a buyer too. Then after a year the owner should lose the right to redeem it. So why does the ברייתא say he can redeem forever?

keyTerms.meaning: Let it make it his forever

phrases.english: But let the Temple treasury keep it forever?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַחְלְטֵיהּ הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule that the owner can always redeem from הקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a buyer keeps the house forever after a year, הקדש should keep it forever too.

steps.title: לדורותיו leaves out הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says לדורותיו, "throughout his generations," which leaves out הקדש, because הקדש has no generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "throughout his generations." This leaves out הקדש, which has no generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the same פסוק. Only a buyer with generations keeps the house forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the house stays with the buyer and his children after him. הקדש is not a person and has no children. So the forever rule does not apply to it, and the owner can always redeem.

keyTerms.meaning: Throughout his generations
Leaves out (is not included)
Generations, descendants

steps.whatToRemember: A house in a walled city given to הקדש: הקדש itself never keeps it forever (לדורותיו), but a person who buys it from הקדש does keep it forever after a year (לקונה אותו).

phrases.english: The verse says: "throughout his generations,"
this leaves out the Temple treasury,
which has no generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״לְדוֹרוֹתָיו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge with another word from the same פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exclusion from a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הקדש should keep the house forever after a year, like any buyer.
steps.terutzMaskana: לדורותיו limits the rule to a buyer who has generations, so הקדש is left out.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק need 'it shall not go out in the יובל'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק adds 'לא יצא ביובל' when it already said the walled-city house belongs to the buyer forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the words 'it shall not go out in the יובל'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the end of the same פסוק and asks what those extra words teach. This sets up רב ספרא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already said the house stays with the buyer 'לצמיתות', forever. If it is his forever, it obviously does not go back in the יובל. So the extra words look unnecessary, and the גמרא wants to know what new thing they add.

keyTerms.meaning: The fiftieth year, when sold land normally goes back to its original owner
'Why do I need it?' This asks what an extra word or phrase is there to teach

phrases.english: 'It shall not go out in the Jubilee':
phrases.notes: This is the end of ויקרא 25:30, right after the words 'forever, to the one who bought it, throughout his generations.'

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יֵצֵא בַּיּוֹבֵל, לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same פסוק (לקונה אותו לדורותיו) and now asks about its last phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case the extra words 'לא יצא ביובל' are needed for.

steps.title: The words cover a sale where the יובל arrives within the first year
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא says the phrase is needed when a walled-city house is sold and the יובל comes during the first year. Without it, we might think the house goes back in the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: It is needed only for someone who sells a house in a walled city, and the יובל comes during his year. You might have thought the house should go back in the יובל. So the פסוק teaches us: 'It shall not go out in the יובל.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא gives a specific case where the extra words teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the first year the sale is not yet final, because the seller can still redeem the house. So we might think the יובל, which returns ordinary fields, should return this house too. The פסוק says no: the יובל does not take it back, even in that first year.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is needed only for…', which points to the one case a phrase is teaching
Houses in cities that are surrounded by a wall
'You might have thought…', the mistaken first idea
'It teaches us', the new point that corrects the mistaken idea

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
It is needed only
for one who sells a house among the houses of walled cities,
and the Jubilee reached it within its year.
It would enter your mind to say:
let it go out in the Jubilee,
so it teaches us:
'It shall not go out in the Jubilee.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why the extra phrase is needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase is needed for a sale where the יובל comes during the first year; even then the house does not go back to the seller.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the walled-city house never goes back in the יובל, not even while the redemption year is still running.

steps.title: Buyers used to hide on the last day of the year
steps.stepSummary: The משנה reports that buyers used to hide on the last day of the twelve months, so the seller could not pay them and the house would become theirs forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: At first, the buyer would hide on the last day of the twelve months, so that the house would become his forever.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes a trick buyers used, and this sets up הלל's fix in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller can redeem only by paying the buyer within twelve months. If the buyer could not be found, the seller could not pay, and the year ran out. The house then became the buyer's for good.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה being studied
Hid himself
Permanently and finally his

phrases.english: MISHNA: At first,

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה נִטְמָן יוֹם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: he would hide on the day of the twelve months,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the buyer, and 'the day' is the last day of the twelve months.

phrases.english: so that it would be his permanently.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיָה נִטְמָן יוֹם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about the same law of walled-city houses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Buyers would hide at the end of the year so the seller could not redeem the house.

steps.title: הלל's תקנה: put the money in the chamber and take the house back
steps.stepSummary: הלל made a rule that the seller may leave the money in the court's chamber, break the door, and go into his house. The buyer can collect the money whenever he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: הלל made a תקנה: the seller leaves his money in the chamber, breaks the door and goes in, and whenever the buyer wants, he can come and take his money.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives הלל's solution to the hiding trick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the seller does not need the buyer to be present. Leaving the money with the court counts as paying, so the redemption works even though the buyer never agreed to take the money.

keyTerms.meaning: Made a rabbinic תקנה, a new enactment
Puts down or deposits money
A chamber, here the court's room where money was kept
'That one', meaning the buyer

phrases.english: Hillel instituted
that he would deposit his money in the chamber,
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the seller, who wants his house back.

phrases.english: and he would break the door and enter,
whenever that other one wishes,
he may come and take his money.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתְקִין הִלֵּל שֶׁיְּהֵא חוֹלֵשׁ מְעוֹתָיו לַלִּשְׁכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the fix for the problem described in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Depositing the money in the court's chamber counts as redeeming the house, even without the buyer.
steps.whatToRemember: Because of הלל's תקנה, a buyer cannot block the redemption of a walled-city house by hiding.

steps.title: רבא: a גט given on condition of payment needs the husband's consent to the payment
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from הלל's תקנה that giving money against someone's will normally does not count. So if a גט depends on a payment, she is divorced only if he accepts the money willingly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From הלל's תקנה we learn: if a man says 'Here is your גט on condition that you give me two hundred זוז,' and she gives it to him with his consent, she is divorced. If she gives it against his will, she is not divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא, who draws a lesson from the משנה and applies it to divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל had to make a special תקנה to let the seller pay without the buyer agreeing. That shows that, without such a תקנה, money forced on someone against his will is not real giving. So the condition of the גט is met only if the husband accepts the money willingly.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic enactment
A bill of divorce
On condition that
With his consent
Against his will

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the גט case is like הלל's case. He is learning the opposite: since הלל needed a special תקנה, the normal rule is that forced payment does not count.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rava said:
From the ordinance of Hillel we learn:
'This is your bill of divorce

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז״,
phrases.english: on condition that you give me two hundred dinars,'
and she gave it to him with his consent: she is divorced;
against his will: she is not divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִתַּקָּנָתוֹ שֶׁל הַלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from the תקנה in the משנה and applies it to divorce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money given against the receiver's will does not meet a condition of giving, so the גט takes effect only if he accepts the money willingly.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a special rule about houses into a general rule about conditions that require giving money.
